I’ve seen enough people ask that I’ll break down the math. 

Brandon Aubrey XP%: 97%
NFL average 2Pt rate: 48%

Key assumptions: You score twice and get stops. OT win probability is 50%

If you kick the XP twice, you have a 95% chance of sending game to OT, 50% chance of winning in OT. 47.5% chance at winning the game.

If you go for two:

Get first, kick XP on second and win in regulation: 46.6% of time, win 100%

Get first, miss XP and go to OT: 1.4% of time, win 50%

Miss first, get second and go to OT: 24.9% of time, win 50% of time

Miss first and second 2-Point: 27.6% of time, guaranteed loss

By going for two, your win probability jumps to 59.8% chance.

So if you guarantee me we get two scores and two stops, you’ll win ~47% of the time kicking extra points, and ~60% of the time going for two.

The reason it doesn’t jive with coaches/fans is because delaying a loss feels psychologically advantageous… but losing in OT vs losing in regulation is the same result
